_comment: Describes how each checkpoint must be preprocessed at inference time.
infer.load_model() and infer.preprocess() read from here rather than from
literals in the source, which is what let training and inference drift
apart (F-01). Every new run writes an entry via train.save_checkpoint().
WARNING: the four 2023 checkpoints below were trained and evaluated with
the bugs described in potential-fixes.md (F-01 through F-10) still live.
Their `metrics` fields record what was *reported* in 2023, not what a
correct harness measures. Run `python evaluate.py --all` to fill in

unetpp_effb0_inria_20260903.pt.note: THE SHIPPED MODEL. Labels are building footprints, not installable area — apply a packing factor downstream and say 'estimated'.

metrics_verified.harness: scripts/eval_inria.py — pooled (global) intersection/union over the whole split, which is the metric the Inria benchmark itself reports
metrics_verified.splits: Inria official protocol — tiles 1-5 per city held out (25 val tiles, 2025 windows at 512 stride 512)

val_as_trained.note: the shipped default before the 2026-09-04 threshold/TTA sweep

_per_window_mean.note: The number training reported. It is a MEAN OF PER-WINDOW IoUs, which weights a window holding one small roof the same as a dense one and so reads low. Pooled IoU (0.7712 at the same threshold) is the comparable-to-literature figure. Both are of the same model on the same split.

limitations: Trained on five Western cities only: austin, chicago, kitsap (WA), tyrol-w, vienna.
Untested on dense low-rise Indian, African or East-Asian rooftops.
Expects ~0.3 m/px imagery; serve at Web Mercator z=19.

unetpp_effb0_inria_spt96_20260906.pt.note: THE BEST INRIA MODEL, AND DELIBERATELY NOT THE DEFAULT. Identical to the shipped model except samples-per-tile 48 -> 96, i.e. twice as many training windows from the same 155 tiles. That bought +0.0131 pooled Inria IoU and cost a fifth of the little Indian recall the shipped model had: footprint recall 0.241 -> 0.191, silent fraction 0.56 -> 0.72, detected area 0.70x -> 0.45x the OpenStreetMap reference. More Western data makes a more Western model. Promote it only if the deployment target is genuinely Inria-like.

metrics_verified.harness: scripts/eval_inria.py (pooled IoU, 25 official val tiles) and scripts/eval_india_osm.py (CV Raman Nagar, Bangalore, 142 OSM footprints)

_per_window_mean.note: what the training loop printed; the shipped model's comparable figure is 0.7233

limitations: Regresses Indian recall relative to the shipped model — the opposite of the project's stated priority.
Trained on the same five Western cities; more data from them, not more places.

joint_v2_india10_20260907.pt.note: Inria plus 505 Indian tiles from TEN cities (402 machine-labelled from Google Open Buildings across eight new cities, plus the 103 OSM-relabelled Bangalore/Bhopal tiles), repeated 8x for ~35% of each epoch. THE FIRST MODEL IN THIS PROJECT TO IMPROVE INDIA WITHOUT PAYING FOR IT ON INRIA: 0.7690 pooled against the shipped 0.7712, a 0.0022 cost that is inside measurement noise, while the silent fraction on held-out blocks falls from 0.744 to 0.080 (Delhi), 0.538 to 0.154 (Mumbai) and 0.379 to 0.081 (Chennai). Every earlier model bought one number at the other's expense - see facts 30 and 31.

metrics_verified.harness: scripts/eval_inria.py (pooled IoU, 25 official val tiles) and scripts/eval_india_osm.py on blocks disjoint from every training AOI

india_heldout_blocks_at_0.50._note: Blocks disjoint from all training AOIs. OSM-anchored RECALL only - OSM is incomplete in India, so precision and IoU here measure the reference, not the model (fact 28).

bangalore_cvraman_CONTAMINATED._warning: NOT a held-out number. bangalore_cvraman_a fully contains the CV Raman Nagar benchmark block and all 30 of its tiles are in this model's training set, because train_inria.py --extra-data-dir holds nothing out. The same is true of joint_v3. Only finetune_osm (which used --holdout-aoi bangalore_cvraman_a) has a clean Bangalore number. Use the held-out city blocks above instead.

limitations: Merges adjacent roofs into single blobs in dense blocks, so building COUNT is less reliable than area.
Indian evaluation is OSM-anchored recall on machine-labelled training regions; no hand-drawn eval set exists for the eight new cities.

Predicts ~2x the detected area of the shipped model in India. Coverage analysis says that is more correct, not less (shipped predicts 11.5% of a dense Delhi block as roof against a realistic 40-60%), but it has not been verified against hand-drawn ground truth.

joint_v3_effb0_20260906.pt.note: Joint training on Inria plus all 103 OSM-relabelled Indian tiles (repeated 20x, ~22% of each epoch). It DID solve the forgetting problem the fine-tunes have — Inria 0.7662 against the shipped 0.7712, where fine-tuning costs ~0.16 — but it captured only about a third of the Indian gain that fine-tuning on the same tiles gets (footprint recall 0.390 vs finetune_osm's 0.716) and left the silent fraction untouched at 0.56. Not promoted: it inflates detected area to 1.28x the OSM reference while its Bangalore IoU does not improve, which is a poor trade for an app that multiplies area into money.

metrics_verified.harness: scripts/eval_inria.py (pooled IoU, 25 official val tiles) and scripts/eval_india_osm.py (CV Raman Nagar, Bangalore, 142 OSM footprints)

repeat_run_noise.note: joint_effb0_20260905.pt and this checkpoint are, as far as the surviving artifacts show, two executions of the SAME configuration — identical epoch size and training loss to four decimals over 46 epochs, best_val_iou differing by 7e-6. Treat the pair as a noise estimate, not a comparison: Inria reproduces to ~0.0001 while the Bangalore figures move ~0.02 (pixel recall 0.460 vs 0.443, footprint recall 0.369 vs 0.390, silent 0.546 vs 0.560). An Indian difference under 0.02 from one run means nothing. A claim that one of them trained on 16 tiles rather than 103 could NOT be substantiated — no such training log survives in the repo.

limitations: Detects 1.28x the OpenStreetMap reference area in Bangalore, and OSM's incompleteness means that cannot be verified as correct.
Bangalore precision 0.347 breaks the ~0.49 that every other model scores there, so the extra area is not simply unmapped buildings.
Recall by size is erratic — the 200-500 m2 band regressed (0.462 -> 0.231) while 0-50 m2 improved.

metrics_verified.harness: evaluate.py, model.eval() on (F-03), no empty-tile inversion (F-08)
evaluate.py, model.eval() on (F-03), no empty-tile inversion (F-08)

metrics_reported_2023.note: Measured with BatchNorm in TRAIN mode (F-03) and with the empty-tile IoU inversion (F-08). Not a valid measurement.

metrics_verified.harness: evaluate.py, model.eval() on (F-03), no empty-tile inversion (F-08)
evaluate.py, model.eval() on (F-03), no empty-tile inversion (F-08)

finetune_indian.pt.note: Fine-tuned on 80 hand-labelled tiles from Bangalore and Bhopal. Transforms Indian recall (0.31 -> 0.92 against OpenStreetMap footprints; 0-50 m2 houses 0.08 -> 0.88) but the labels merged adjacent buildings and the alleys between them, so it predicts CLUSTER ENVELOPES, not footprints: predicted area is ~2.1x the footprint model's on the same block. Use packing_factor ~0.5 rather than 0.70-0.75, and do not compare its Inria IoU with 0.7712 - different target. Serve it with RSOLAR_MODEL=finetune_indian.

metrics_verified.harness: scripts/eval_inria.py on 5 Inria val tiles for the regression check; webapp/calibration.py reference calibration against 141 OpenStreetMap footprints in CV Raman Nagar, Bangalore, for the recall figures

inria_5tile.note: Lower than the shipped model BY CONSTRUCTION: an envelope prediction over-covers Inria's footprint labels, which costs precision while recall holds. Not catastrophic forgetting.
inria_5tile.superseded_by: inria_official_val_at_0.50 — a 5-tile subset overstated the regression

inria_official_val_at_0.50.note: Full 25-tile official val split. Still an envelope model scored against footprint labels — read the recall (0.881, essentially the shipped model's) rather than the IoU.

limitations: Predicts building-cluster envelopes, not individual footprints — building COUNT is meaningless and area includes inter-building alleys.
Trained on 80 tiles from two Indian cities; unvalidated anywhere else.
Regresses precision on Western imagery (Inria 5-tile IoU 0.80 -> 0.65).

finetune_osm.pt.note: Fine-tuned on 103 Indian tiles relabelled from OpenStreetMap, with hand-drawn envelopes used as an IGNORE mask (positive = OSM building, ignore = envelope minus OSM, negative = the rest). Preferred over finetune_indian.pt for India: same footprint semantics as the shipped model, so the normal packing factor applies, and far less area inflation (1.37x the OSM reference vs the envelope model's 1.59x). Still regresses Inria (0.639 vs 0.800 on 5 val tiles), so it is not a global default. Serve with RSOLAR_MODEL=finetune_osm.

metrics_verified.harness: Pooled IoU against 142 OpenStreetMap footprints in CV Raman Nagar, Bangalore - an AOI held out of training in full - plus scripts/eval_inria.py on 5 Inria val tiles

bangalore_vs_osm_at_0.50.note: Precision is ~0.49 for every model tested, which measures OpenStreetMap's incompleteness rather than model quality - roughly half of what any model predicts is not mapped.

inria_5tile_at_0.50.superseded_by: inria_official_val_at_0.50 — a 5-tile subset overstated the regression

inria_official_val_at_0.50.note: Full 25-tile official val split. The real cost of fine-tuning is ~0.10 pooled IoU, not the ~0.16 the 5-tile subset suggested.

limitations: Regresses Inria (0.639 vs the shipped 0.800) - fine-tuning on ~100 narrow tiles costs ~0.16 IoU regardless of label source. Joint training (kaggle_joint/) is the fix.
Positives come from OpenStreetMap, which is incomplete here; buildings nobody mapped were marked ignore only where the labeller had drawn an envelope over them.
Trained on two Indian cities; unvalidated anywhere else.

_current_best.split: Inria official protocol — tiles 1-5 per city held out (155 train / 25 val tiles)
_current_best.note: THE SHIPPED MODEL — this is what webapp/ serves. See results/RESULTS.md.

_swiss_best.note: Best on the Swiss DOP25 set (available-roof-area labels). Not comparable to the Inria number — different labels, resolution and country. Kept as a secondary out-of-distribution eval.
